The findings highlight China's dependence on U.S. tech in the face of increasing trade tensions.

This move marks a shift in their previous focus on affluent customers in specific urban areas.

These results led to a sharp decline in both companies' stock prices.

He is recognized for his prolific writing and advocacy for investments in Asia, Latin America, Africa, and other frontier markets.

title: Bank of America Earnings Hurt by Tax-Related Charge
summary: Bank of America reported a 48% drop in quarterly profit due to a $2.9 billion charge related to the new U.S. tax law. Analysts had expected lower earnings on an adjusted basis, but the bank would have surpassed these expectations without the tax charge.

summary: State Street has launched a new low-cost gold exchange-traded fund, the SPDR Gold MiniShares ETF, which aims to be the cheapest on the market. title: In 'Strategic' Natural Gas Combo, Dominion to Buy Scana for $7.9B
summary: Dominion Energy Inc. plans to acquire Scana Corp. in an all-stock deal valued at $7.9 billion in stock and an overall value of about $14.6 billion, creating one of the nation's largest natural gas storage systems. The merger aims to expand Dominion's natural gas business in the Southeast and includes provisions to address customer costs from Scana's abandoned nuclear plant expansion, such as a $1.3 billion cash payment and a 5% rate cut. The deal is contingent on shareholder and regulatory approvals, with Dominion warning it could walk away if adverse changes are imposed.

title: Turkish Luxury Retailer Beymen Said to Explore IPO
summary: Turkish luxury retailer Beymen, a subsidiary of Boyner Perakende, is reportedly exploring an initial public offering (IPO) and is in talks with several major banks, including Bank of America, Citigroup, and Deutsche Bank, to manage the sale. Boyner Perakende plans to offer up to 49 percent of Beymen, which distributes approximately 600 international fashion brands across more than 80 outlets in Turkey. This potential IPO follows a significant increase in IPO activity in Turkey in the previous year.

title: Investors urge Casey's to sell Iowa-based convenience store chain
summary: A group of Casey's General Stores Inc. investors, including JCP Investment Management LLC, BLR Partners, and shareholder Joshua Schechter, are urging the company to consider selling the convenience store chain, claiming its shares are "significantly undervalued." They contend that Casey's has missed earnings targets due to decelerating same-store sales and bloated operational expenses, and that rapid expansion has led to declining returns on invested capital. Casey's CEO Terry Handley stated the company is focused on increasing shareholder value through same-store growth, share repurchases, and dividends.

The author advises investors to simplify their U.S. equity exposure through total market index funds rather than attempting to combine various market-cap segments.

This decision highlights increased U.S. scrutiny of Chinese investment amid rising tensions between the two nations. The companies cited difficulties in addressing CFIUS concerns despite extensive efforts.

summary: Major banks like Regions, SunTrust, and First Tennessee are attributing recent wage increases, bonuses, and increased investments to the new corporate tax cuts. Regions and SunTrust have raised their minimum wages to $15 an hour and committed significant funds to charitable foundations, community grants, and capital expenditures. These actions are a direct response to the corporate tax rate dropping from 35 percent to 21 percent, with banks anticipating substantial savings.

title: Regions to raise its minimum hourly wage to $15
summary: Regions Financial Corp. announced a series of long-term investments, including raising its minimum hourly wage to $15 by the end of the year, up from its official minimum of $10.15 in 2014. This move will affect about 25 percent of its workforce company-wide, including around 200 employees in the greater Hattiesburg area and 650 statewide. The company also plans to contribute $40 million to its charitable foundation and increase its capital expenditures budget by approximately $100 million due to anticipated savings from federal tax reform.

title: Calif. TJ Maxx, Marshalls, & HomeGoods Deceptive Pricing Settlement
summary: The TJX Companies Inc. agreed to an $8.5 million class action settlement for deceptive pricing practices at T.J. Maxx, HomeGoods, and Marshalls stores in California. The lawsuit alleged that the "Compare At" prices were misleading. Eligible customers who purchased items with a "Compare At" price between July 17, 2011, and Dec. 6, 2017, can claim a merchandise credit or cash.

summary: American Midstream Partners (AMID) announced the full operation of the Cayenne Pipeline, a joint venture with Targa Resources Corp. The pipeline has an initial capacity of 40,000 barrels per day of Y-grade NGL transport, expandable to over 50,000 barrels per day, originating from Targa's Venice gas processing plant. This project enhances AMID's strategic NGL transport capabilities from the Gulf of Mexico's deep-water Mississippi Canyon region and creates value by repurposing an underutilized pipeline.

summary: Cboe Global Markets has launched a new microsite to educate investors about exchange-traded volatility products (ETPs), particularly those linked to derivative indexes of the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX). The microsite aims to help investors understand the risks and rewards of these complex products, which are typically based on rolling long positions in VIX futures. This initiative comes as Cboe continues to expand its ETF Marketplace, having listed 129 ETFs in 2017.

title: Shares in Nutrien rise on 2nd day of trading after analysts publish high ratings
summary: Shares of Nutrien Ltd., the newly formed Canadian fertilizer giant, surged on its second day of trading after CIBC assigned an "outperformer" rating and a US$62 price target. Analysts believe Nutrien could realize significantly more cost-saving synergies than initially estimated from the merger of Agrium Inc. and Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan Inc., potentially reaching US$100-125 million in additional savings. The company's strategy includes expanding its retail footprint in the U.S. and rationalizing wholesale operations, with expected returns to investors through share buybacks and dividends.

summary: Brazil's state-controlled oil company Petrobras agreed to pay $2.95 billion to settle a U.S. class action corruption lawsuit, marking one of the largest securities class action settlements in U.S. history by a foreign entity. The settlement is seen as an important step for Petrobras to move past the "Car Wash" scandal, though it may reduce the likelihood of a dividend payment for 2017. Analysts noted the settlement amount was lower than anticipated by some, and Moody's indicated it would not materially impact the company's balance sheet.

title: US bars Chinese acquisition of MoneyGram
summary: The US government has rejected Chinese billionaire Jack Ma's bid to acquire MoneyGram for US$1.2 billion, citing national security concerns. The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) did not approve the deal despite efforts to address its concerns, leading to a 6.8 per cent drop in MoneyGram shares. This failed acquisition highlights heightened American scrutiny of Chinese investments, similar to a previous rejection of a semiconductor manufacturer acquisition.

title: U.S. blocks MoneyGram sale to China's Ant Financial on national security concerns
summary: The $1.2 billion acquisition of U.S. money transfer company MoneyGram International Inc by China's Ant Financial collapsed due to national security concerns raised by a U.S. government panel. This marks a significant blow to Ant Financial's expansion plans and highlights the U.S. government's toughening stance on Chinese acquisitions of American companies, particularly concerning data security. MoneyGram's shares fell 8.5% in after-market trading following the announcement, although the companies plan to explore future commercial partnerships in various markets.

The merger would create a wireless giant competitive with Verizon and AT&T, but regulators may view the reduction of a major competitor as harmful to pricing competition. Approval is expected to be difficult, especially since it's a horizontal merger which historically faces close scrutiny.

summary: Marathon Petroleum Corp. has agreed to acquire rival oil refiner Andeavor for $23.3 billion, creating the largest independent fuel maker in the United States. This deal will combine Marathon's Midwestern and Gulf Coast presence with Andeavor's Western states operations, forming a company responsible for approximately 16% of the nation's total oil refining capacity. The acquisition is expected to generate $1 billion in annual cost and operating synergies within three years and is projected to close in the second half of the year.

title: Former UBS Insider Says Banks Fueled Economic Crisis in Puerto Rico
summary: A former UBS insider, Carlos Capacete, alleges that banks, including UBS, fueled Puerto Rico's economic crisis by encouraging the government to take on billions in debt, which ultimately led to the island's default and bankruptcy. Capacete claims that Wall Street's role in pushing risky debt has been overlooked, and that banks actively promoted bond sales and risky loan schemes to maximize profits, despite warnings about the island's financial stability. The Securities and Exchange Commission later settled with UBS for $15 million over related allegations, and UBS Puerto Rico has paid over $65 million in regulatory fines while facing numerous customer claims.

title: Over Half of Americans Report Feeling Like No One Knows Them Well
summary: A recent Ipsos survey conducted on behalf of Cigna reveals that over half of Americans (54%) sometimes or always feel as though no one knows them well, indicating widespread feelings of loneliness. The study found consistent traits distinguishing lonely individuals, such as infrequent in-person interactions and poorer overall health, and identified Generation Z as the loneliest age group, with loneliness generally decreasing with age. In-person interactions and good health are strongly linked to lower loneliness scores.

The study comes as an easing of financial regulations is expected to drive more back-office relocations and cost-cutting efforts in the industry.

The move is driven by lower living expenses and taxes in Tennessee compared to New York, and aligns with AllianceBernstein's strategy to achieve ongoing expense savings despite transitional costs.

title: Allstate CEO Wilson Warns AI Will Slam Economy With ‘Tsunami’-Like Force

Despite anticipating challenges in domestic snack and frozen food markets, Morinaga is committed to strengthening its business base, expanding its product offerings, and fostering open innovation to adapt to rapid market changes.
